prompt:
Render a high-fidelity desktop homepage UI mockup for FoodBridge, edge to edge at 1536 by 1024, crisp legible text, no browser frame or device. FoodBridge coordinates surplus food and waste collection in Sri Lanka. Donors, recipient organisations, recyclers, volunteers, and admins deserve equal visibility. The visitor's job is to understand the service and enter the right role. The visual world is a contemporary community wayfinding system: deep leaf-green information fields, clean white and pale mint grounds, sparing sunflower yellow for orientation. Broad humanist sans lettering, generous directional spacing, simple numbered destinations, restrained arrow signs; this is a usable website, not an illustrated street or poster. No fake numbers, testimonials, certifications, maps, current jobs, or impact claims.
Lead with a destination-directory concept. Navigation reads "FoodBridge.", "How it works", "Community impact", "Sign in". The opening joins the compact headline "Good food. Shared responsibility." and the explanation "Food sharing and waste collection in Sri Lanka." directly to one dominant, generously typeset five-row directory; the actions are the homepage's main event, not a row of small cards beneath a generic hero. Use real role actions with equal prominence: "Donor — Share food or post waste"; "Recipient organisation — Register for review"; "Recycler — Register for review"; "Volunteer — Help with pickups"; "Admin — Sign in to manage". Each has a clear clickable arrow or action. Include the readable disclosure "Recipient and recycler browsing and claims are not available yet." Public admin signup must not appear.
The start of the next section is visible below the directory: "From surplus to a recorded outcome", with a quiet documentary photograph of Sri Lankan adults handing a crate of fresh food across a community table. This is illustrative imagery, not proof of an actual delivery. Keep edible food and waste separate. Finish the viewport with enough of this section to demonstrate a real scrolling page and include "View community impact".
